children: President Donald Trump on Tuesday moved to fill an additional judicial vacancy before Democrats take control of the Senate, nominating a Republican North Carolina district attorney to become a life-tenured federal judge after he lost his re-election bid in the state.

Trump, in a post on his social media platform Truth Social, said he is nominating Jim O’Neill to serve on the US District Court for the Middle District of North Carolina with the support of both of his state's Republican senators, including outgoing Senator Thom Tillis.

Tillis, a member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, complicated Trump's judicial appointment push in recent weeks along with other Republicans by blocking the White House's preferred picks for judges in their states from advancing in the Senate.
"He has a deep track record of being tough on crime and preserving Law and Order," Trump said of O'Neill.

The White House and Senate Republican leaders have been racing to confirm as many of Trump's remaining judicial nominees as possible before Democrats on January 3 take control of the Senate after winning a 56-seat majority in the November 3 election.
Trump, between his two terms in office, has secured the appointment of 295 judicial nominees to lifetime positions, including three members of the US Supreme Court's 6-3 conservative majority.
O'Neill has served as the district attorney of North Carolina's Forsyth County, home to Winston-Salem, since 2009. He lost his bid for a fifth term in November to Democrat Amara Hunter.
Trump had previously endorsed O'Neill during his 2020 race to become North Carolina's attorney general, which he lost to Democrat Josh Stein, who is now the state's governor.

Trump's announcement came a day after Reuters on Monday reported that the White House had initiated FBI background checks on a Tillis-backed judicial nominee in North Carolina as well as a potential replacement for a would-be judge in Texas whose nomination was blocked by outgoing Republican Senator John Cornyn.

The decision signaled the White House is considering nominating Steve Fahey, Cornyn's preferred pick to be a federal judge in Dallas, in place of Justice Department official T. Elliot Gaiser. But Trump has not announced any change in nomination strategy in Texas.
Nineteen other judicial nominees remain pending besides Gaiser and O'Neill.
